title: AssessmentBattery
description: The ordered capture steps of an assessment, as data, so the app, backend and analysis agree on what each step records and which metrics it can produce. Draft until a clinical lead signs it off.

instruction.description: Shown and spoken to the person being assessed.

requiresSpotter.description: True when a member of staff must be within arm's reach for the whole step (HZ-09, induced fall). This is NOT advisory: a step with this set cannot reach recording until a clinician has confirmed presence, and the server refuses a clip for such a step with no confirmation recorded for that session and step. See docs/hazard-analysis.md HZ-09, whose own bar is that a control is structurally enforced rather than documented.

eyesClosed.description: True when the person is asked to close their eyes. Removes visual balance correction, so it raises fall risk independently of stance and is the main reason a step would set requiresSpotter.

stance.description: Base of support. single_left means standing on the person's LEFT leg. Named per side rather than as a generic 'single_leg' because the two are different measurements and a report that pooled them would be comparing different limbs.

contraindications.description: Clinician-authored conditions under which this step must not be offered. Same shape as protocol-definition.schema.json's field of the same name, deliberately: a clinician writing one should not have to learn two formats. Free text because the authority is the clinician, not an enum this repo maintains.

subBlocks.description:
Splits one continuous recording into named sub-phases, so a single clip can carry a relaxed hold, a habitual stance settled into after marching, and an AR-standardised stance without being three separate uploads. Omit for an ordinary single-phase hold.

The recording does NOT stop between sub-blocks: the camera runs throughout and each frame is tagged with the sub-phase it fell in (clip-capture.schema.json's frames[].subPhase), so the analysis gets deterministic boundaries instead of having to split the clip by heuristic. Only `instruction` and the cue change at a boundary.

The step's own `durationSeconds` stays authoritative and MUST equal the sum of the sub-block durations. JSON Schema cannot express that sum, so BatteryService checks it at boot and refuses to start on a mismatch - see its loader.

phase.description: relaxed: stand as you normally would, no prompting. habitual: the stance the person settles into by themselves, captured after marching in place so it is not the one they were posed in. standardized: feet placed to the AR template, so between-visit comparisons share a base of support. Each value may appear at most once per step; BatteryService rejects a duplicate.

instruction.description: Shown and spoken at the start of this sub-phase.

preparation.description: What the person does to get into this sub-phase before its timer starts, e.g. "march in place for five steps". Separate from `instruction` because this part is not being recorded as measurement - it is what makes the following stance habitual rather than posed.

symptomStopRules.description: Clinician-authored plain-language stop/escalate instructions surfaced on a SymptomReport, mirroring protocol-definition.schema.json. These do NOT gate anything on their own: every symptom report reaches Pause regardless of what any rule says (CLAUDE.md rule 2), and these are what a clinician reads afterwards.

allOf.$comment: Sub-blocks only make sense inside a continuous hold. A reps or passes step has its own natural segmentation and splitting it by time would cut across repetitions.

A step that asks for eyes closed, or for a single-leg stance, MUST require a spotter. Encoded in the schema rather than left to the author because this is the structural half of HZ-09: a battery that asked for a one-legged eyes-closed hold without a spotter would fail to load (BatteryService throws on a battery that does not validate) rather than reaching a patient.
